o1.biggest_strength: It gives the right straight answer on the 20% cut, shows the lifetime value math clearly, and focuses the programme around the top creator-educator partners instead of chasing more inactive affiliates.
o1.biggest_mistake: The 40% first-year Partner tier is plausible, but the cost model is a little rough and could overpay top partners without a tighter cap or review rule.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Tighten the Partner tier eligibility and budget controls, model the 90-day credit-window cost more carefully, and make the day-90 review criteria a bit more operational.

o2.biggest_strength: The plan understands the real problem: this is a partner-retention and attribution issue, not a commission-rate issue. The 'Who sent you?' attribution test is a strong extra idea.
o2.biggest_mistake: Some of the cost math is shaky, especially the projected cost of the 90-day window and the year-one savings from cutting only new referrals. I would not want to take those numbers to finance without reworking them.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Fix the financial model, narrow the Partner tier so one manager can run it well, and fold the survey-attribution idea into the main plan instead of making it feel like an add-on.

reason: I would use Output 1 sooner because it is more complete, cleaner, and more reliable on the numbers. Output 2 has one excellent attribution idea, but I would need to check and rewrite more before sending it around.
